subject: Errors and unexpected results with a space-time LGCP

messages.author: 263f1fc934267fff
messages.subject: Errors and unexpected results with a space-time LGCP
parts:
Dear Group,

I'm trying to estimate the effect of different covariates on the density of a bird species in space and time. Data set consists in the "complete" (as a first approximation) locations of individuals over 5 consecutive years (I'm planning to include more years once I'll have the environmental covariates).

I was planning to use space-time LGCP (based on the examples provided by the SPDE tutorial) to model the intensity of the replicated point patterns but I encountered several issues I wasn't able to solve.

The model without covariate (spde with ar1 autoregressive structure) ran smoothly  ~5' on a Intel Xeon 6 cores, 3.2 GHz, with 16 Go of RAM).
Once I included covariate into the models, I noticed some weird behaviours, such as errors of the following type appearing repeatedly during the estimation process

"file: smtp-taucs.c  hgid: 755a4114e167  date: Wed Aug 19 15:24:56 2015 +0200
        Function: GMRFLib_build_sparse_matrix_TAUCS(), Line: 712, Thread: 0
        Variable evaluates to NAN or INF. idx=(257,257). I will try to fix it...Max.post.marg(theta): log(dens) = -3983.355015 fn = 43 theta =  -0.840456 -1.900103 5.017968
Max.post.marg(theta): log(dens) = -3983.159031 fn = 44 theta =  -0.840456 -1.910103 5.017968"

as well as an overal increase of processing time. Covariates have been scaled (xsi=(xi-mean(x))/sd(x)) to keep them on approximately the same scale and I also tried to specify proper priors as suggested in this thread but it didn't improve the fitting.

As I was afraid of mispecifying the mesh, I asked for advises a couple of weeks ago and Elias was kind enough to provide me with a mesh that seems right. So there shouldn't be a problem with that.

I don't want to give up but I doubt I'll be able to solve this problem on my own. One can find some outputs of the different runs I tried in this document and I can provide any generous soul with the data if necessary.

Thanks in advance for your help /  assistance and have a nice week end.

Best regards

Alex

messages.author: b453c29749de564d
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Errors and unexpected results with a space-time LGCP
parts:
Hi,

what you have is that something in the latent field is going towards
infinity. this is usually some kind of confounding (or almost so). 
try to set more informative priors, like 

control.fixed = list(prec = 1, prec.intercept = 1)

just to check, and maybe more informative for the precision of the
latent field driving the lgcp

Best
H

Dear Havard,

Thanks for your advices. The more informative priors on the fixed
effects part did not help and I got the same issues with ar1 spde /
temporal replicates (I also tried the same type of models but this
time without the AR1 structure) as soon as I added a covariate.
When running models year by year, everything seems to go fine with
relatively uninformative priors control.fixed = list(prec = 0.001,
prec.intercept = 0.001)

and the results are in accordance with what I would have expected.

Regarding your suggestion of more informative prior for the precision
of the latent field, I would specify this in the theta.prior.prec
option of the inla.spde2.matern() function, right?
How much informative these priors should be? I guess this depends on
the data as well but I have difficulties figuring out how far I can
push.

In the mean time, I'll continue searching by myself, and anyway,
thanks again for your help

Alex
